review: 1:1–1:4 רֹפֵא נַפְשִׁי … מַרְפֵּא — the Arabic شَخْصُهُ طَبِيبُ نَفْسِي / صَوْتُهُ أَيْضًا عِلَاج sets the person against the voice; Hebrew keeps the same parallel with the noun מַרְפֵּא (the healing, as in Jer 8:22), not the Modern Hebrew תְּרוּפָה.

4:4 וְהָאֲהוּבִים בַּדּוֹד — the Arabic وَالْأَحِبَّا بِالْحَبِيب is 'and the loved ones in the Beloved'; בַּדּוֹד keeps the preposition of union (as in Song 2:16, דּוֹדִי לִי), so the line is not merely 'the beloved ones'.
3:3 עַיִן בְּעָיִן — the Arabic بِالْعِيَانِ is 'plainly, face to face'; the Hebrew idiom (Num 14:14) keeps the sight physical, which is what the stanza asks for.

2:3–2:4 וּבְכָל־קָרְבִי אֵלָיו / יוֹסִיף עֶרְגָּתִי — the Arabic كُلَّمَا أَدْنُو لَدَيْهِ / زَادَنِي لَهُ اشْتِيَاق is the paradox 'the nearer, the more longing'; the Hebrew keeps both comparatives implicit and lets the two lines carry the turn.
